shortDescription: Wall Street has rediscovered the buy button, AI demand remains enormous and Treasury yields are finally cooperating📈 Stocks attempt a broader recovery🤖 Broadcom keeps the AI trade running👷 Payrolls hold the final vote

children: Wall Street has rediscovered the buy button, AI demand remains enormous and Treasury yields are finally cooperating
Stocks attempt a broader recovery

S&P 500 futures climbed roughly 0.5% Thursday, while Nasdaq contracts added around 0.2%. Wednesday’s cash session ended a three-day losing streak: the S&P 500 gained 0.5%, the Nasdaq rose 0.5% and the Dow advanced 295 points, or 0.6%.
The Russell 2000 outperformed with a 1.1% gain, while regional banks, airlines and precious-metal miners joined the recovery.
That healthier breadth was a big positive because it shows investors buying beyond mega-cap technology. Nvidia still provided substantial assistance, naturally, rising 3.2%.
Dell surged 15.8% after
to $192 billion, supported by a $95 billion AI-server backlog.
Snowflake then jumped more than 23% after hours following strong results and improved guidance. Artificial intelligence apparently remains disruptive — particularly to analysts’ spreadsheets.
Broadcom keeps the AI trade running

Broadcom reported third-quarter revenue of $29.59 billion as AI-chip sales rocketed 221% to $16.7 billion. Adjusted earnings reached $3.32 per share, while management raised its AI-chip revenue outlook to approximately $115 billion in 2027 and $230 billion in 2028.
The immediate forecast was slightly less heroic. Broadcom guided fourth-quarter revenue to $34.8 billion, just below Wall Street’s $35.03 billion estimate.
That mixed reception leaves Nasdaq futures subdued despite spectacular longer-term numbers. At current valuations, doubling eventually is encouraging; beating next quarter remains compulsory.
Retreating Treasury yields are giving growth stocks additional support after the ten-year yield recently approached 5%.

Higher yields reduce the present value of distant corporate profits and make bonds more competitive with equities. Below that threshold, the market can breathe. Near it, every valuation model develops asthma.
Payrolls hold the final vote
Weak private-sector hiring has increased the stakes around Friday’s nonfarm payrolls report, expected to show roughly 56,000 new jobs.
Markets currently price around a 60%–65% chance of a September Fed rate increase, leaving stocks unusually sensitive to employment, wages and unemployment.
Asian equities followed Wall Street higher, while a firmer yen reflected growing expectations for another Bank of Japan rate hike.
Gold rebounded more than 1% toward $4,435 (kudos to all who got onboard) as the dollar and yields softened. Those moves suggest traders are reducing rate risk, although Friday still owns the eraser.
Brent crude eased toward $95 and WTI slipped below $91 after the latest US-Iran exchange produced no immediate follow-up attack. Oil remains elevated enough to complicate inflation, however.

title: SPX: S&P 500 Futures Rise and Bond Yields Retreat Before Key Jobs Report
